agenda: The situation in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: The United States aims to secure Council action on unimpeded humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and a peaceful democratic path forward in Venezuela while avoiding language that would trigger a Russian or Chinese veto. The main difficulty is that Russia and China oppose any text that could be read as challenging the Maduro government or calling for new elections, so the draft is deliberately balanced and omits explicit recognition of interim President Guaidó. We expect at least nine affirmative votes from the United States, France, the United Kingdom, and key non-permanent members, with Russia and China likely abstaining rather than vetoing.

messages.Belgium: Belgium supports the draft as a balanced basis for Council action. It addresses the humanitarian emergency, unimpeded access, protection of civilians and the need for a peaceful, Venezuelan-led political process leading to free, fair and transparent elections, while reaffirming sovereignty and non-interference. We would not reopen the text and urge all members to support it.
messages.China: The current draft remains unbalanced and risks being used to exert pressure on Venezuela, which is an internal matter for the Venezuelan people. China cannot support it as it stands. We require clear language opposing external interference, military intervention and unilateral sanctions, and ensuring humanitarian assistance respects Venezuela's sovereignty and is provided with its consent. The references to obstruction and a 30-day reporting requirement should be balanced or removed.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire supports the humanitarian thrust of the draft but can only support it if it is clearly anchored in respect for Venezuela’s sovereignty and non-interference and explicitly excludes any military intervention. We also need humanitarian assistance to be delivered in coordination with the competent national authorities and the political track to be Venezuelan-led, inclusive and without preconditions. With these adjustments, we would be in a position to support the draft.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic supports the draft as a balanced and appropriate response to the crisis, which prioritizes humanitarian access, peaceful dialogue and respect for Venezuela's sovereignty. We urge all Council members to support it and call on all parties in Venezuela to refrain from violence and allow safe, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the draft’s humanitarian and dialogue objectives, but we cannot accept language that could be read as authorizing external intervention or external pressure on Venezuela’s sovereign political process. We therefore ask the penholder to strengthen OP6 and to make clear that humanitarian access and dialogue are carried out with respect for Venezuela’s sovereignty and in coordination with its authorities. With these changes, Equatorial Guinea can support the text.
messages.France: France supports the draft’s balanced focus on humanitarian access, protection of civilians and a peaceful political solution. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP4 by specifying presidential elections, held without delay and with international observation, so that the text addresses the root cause of the crisis. France will support the resolution once this clarification is made.
messages.Germany: Germany supports the draft as a balanced and humanitarian-focused basis for Council action. We particularly welcome the emphasis on safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, protection of civilians, human rights, and a peaceful, Venezuelan-led political solution. We urge all Council members to unite behind this text and call on all parties in Venezuela to comply in good faith.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia appreciates the draft's focus on humanitarian access and peaceful dialogue. We would need OP4 to affirm a Venezuelan-led and Venezuelan-owned process free from external interference. Humanitarian assistance should be neutral, non-politicized and coordinated with the host authorities; without these changes Indonesia would have difficulty supporting the text.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait supports the current balanced text. It properly emphasizes sovereignty, non-interference, humanitarian access in accordance with humanitarian principles, and a peaceful, Venezuelan-led dialogue. We have no changes to request at this stage and are ready to support the draft.
messages.Peru: Peru supports the balanced draft and welcomes the inclusion of sovereignty, non-interference and humanitarian principles. We ask that OP4 explicitly refer to free, fair, transparent and credible presidential elections and to the restoration of democratic institutional order, since this is central to a peaceful solution. With that refinement, Peru is prepared to support the text.
messages.Poland: Poland supports the draft as a balanced and constructive basis. We request that OP4 explicitly refer to new free, fair, transparent and credible presidential elections, since the 2018 presidential election did not meet international standards. We are flexible on the precise wording and remain ready to support the text.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support this draft as it stands: it creates a legal and political basis for external humanitarian deliveries without the consent of the legitimate Venezuelan authorities and for imposing electoral outcomes from outside. We will table amendments requiring the consent and coordination of the Government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, deleting language on obstruction that prejudges responsibility, and removing any call for elections or Security Council reporting that interferes in Venezuela’s internal affairs. If these red lines are not reflected, we will not support the text and will use our veto if necessary.
messages.South Africa: South Africa cannot support the draft as it stands. We welcome the humanitarian emphasis, but the text must clearly reject any threat or use of force and any external interference, and it must frame elections as a Venezuelan-led decision rather than an external prescription. We also ask that humanitarian access be in full respect for Venezuela's sovereignty and that the text call for lifting unilateral coercive measures that worsen the humanitarian crisis.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the draft resolution as a balanced and appropriate response to the grave situation in Venezuela. We welcome its focus on unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians and a peaceful, democratic political process leading to free and fair elections. We urge all Council members to support the text and call for its swift adoption.

steps.summary: The revised text balances US priorities on humanitarian access, human rights, and a democratic political process with concerns about sovereignty, non-interference, and non-militarization. Key compromises include Venezuelan-led dialogue, anti-force language, and coordination with authorities, while retaining presidential elections and a 30-day report. The draft is expected to secure 12 votes in favour, with South Africa opposed and China and Russia abstaining, avoiding a P5 veto.

messages.Belgium: Belgium supports the current draft as a balanced and credible basis. It captures our priorities on humanitarian access, human rights, accountability, inclusive dialogue and the rejection of any military intervention, while respecting Venezuela's sovereignty. We have no further changes to request and would vote in favour if the text is put to the vote.
messages.China: China appreciates the partial acceptance of sovereignty and anti-force language, but the current text still does not meet our red lines. It must explicitly require the consent of and coordination with the Government of Venezuela for humanitarian assistance and must reject unilateral sanctions and external interference. China also cannot accept language that prescribes elections; this is for Venezuelans to decide through inclusive dialogue. Without these changes China cannot support the text and would vote against it.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire welcomes the incorporation of sovereignty, the rejection of force and coordination with national authorities. We can support the text if OP4 explicitly states that dialogue is without preconditions and supported by regional mediation mechanisms where appropriate. This is essential to keep the process genuinely Venezuelan-led and to avoid the appearance of externally prescribed political outcomes.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic supports the draft as presented. It reflects the priority we attach to unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians, and a peaceful, Venezuelan-led dialogue, while respecting Venezuela's sovereignty and territorial integrity. We appreciate the penholder's balanced text and are prepared to vote in favor.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea appreciates the penholder's partial incorporation of our concerns, particularly on sovereignty, coordination with national authorities and Venezuelan ownership. However, our red line remains: the text must explicitly reject any external interference and any attempt at regime change in Venezuela, not only military intervention. Without that language, my delegation cannot support the draft and will abstain.
messages.France: France welcomes the penholder's efforts and the partial acceptance of our OP4 proposal. We remain concerned that, without a clear timeline, OP4 could be read as allowing indefinite delay in presidential elections; France therefore asks to insert 'without delay' after 'presidential elections' and to delete 'as appropriate' from international observation. With those refinements, France can support the text, and we underline our support for OP6's rejection of any threat or use of force and external military intervention.
messages.Germany: Germany supports the current text as a balanced and appropriate response to the crisis in Venezuela. It addresses humanitarian access, the need to protect civilians and the importance of a peaceful, Venezuelan-led political solution with credible elections. Germany asks for no further changes and encourages the Council to adopt the resolution without delay.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia supports the revised text as a basis and welcomes the incorporation of Venezuelan-led dialogue and the non-politicization of humanitarian assistance. To fully anchor the principle of non-interference, we ask that OP4 explicitly state that the dialogue is conducted without external interference. We also prefer OP3 to invite, as appropriate, rather than call upon Member States, so humanitarian action remains voluntary and coordinated with the UN and Venezuelan authorities. With these adjustments, Indonesia is ready to support the resolution.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait supports the humanitarian objectives and the call for a peaceful, Venezuelan-led solution, but the current text remains ambiguous on consent and could be read as endorsing parallel authorities. We request that OP2 and OP3 refer explicitly to the Government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela and that OP4 make international observation conditional on the request and consent of that Government. Without these changes, Kuwait will abstain.
messages.Peru: Peru supports the draft and appreciates the penholder's partial acceptance of our OP4 amendment by retaining presidential elections. For Peru, the text would be stronger and more balanced if OP4 also referenced the restoration of democratic institutional order, in line with the Venezuelan Constitution and the will of the Venezuelan people. We ask the penholder to insert that phrase as proposed; we can support the text with this addition.
messages.Poland: Poland welcomes the penholder’s partial acceptance and can support the draft with this clarification. We continue to believe that the word 'new' is necessary to make clear that the Council is not conferring legitimacy on the 2018 process and that the solution requires fresh, credible presidential elections. This remains an important point for our delegation.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support the current draft. It still fails to require the consent of the legitimate Government of Venezuela for humanitarian assistance, retains election benchmarks and a reporting mechanism that intrude into Venezuela's sovereignty, and does not clearly reject regime change or external interference. Unless these red lines are reflected, we will vote against the draft.
messages.South Africa: South Africa appreciates the inclusion of anti-force language and Venezuelan-led dialogue, but cannot support the text as it remains unbalanced. The absence of any reference to lifting unilateral coercive measures, which aggravate the humanitarian situation, is a red line for us. We also seek explicit coordination with the Government of Venezuela and the removal of open-ended international election observation to fully respect sovereignty.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the aims of this draft and will work for a consensus outcome, but we cannot accept language that gives the Maduro authorities a veto over humanitarian access. OP2 must make clear that assistance is delivered without political conditions or undue restrictions, and OP4 should call for elections without delay with full international observation. We would also want a preambular reference to the flawed 2018 presidential election.

reasons.Belgium: Belgium had already signalled support for this balanced draft, which aligns with its priorities on humanitarian access, dialogue, sovereignty and the peaceful settlement of disputes. Voting in favour is consistent with Belgium’s EU-aligned position and its support for a negotiated political solution.
reasons.China: China’s core red lines—consent and coordination with the Venezuelan Government on aid, opposition to external interference, and rejection of externally mandated elections—were not met. As a P5 member aligned with sovereignty/non-interference and Maduro’s government, China would vote against and likely explain its veto.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire had already indicated support_with_changes and its requested OP4 language was accepted; the draft’s emphasis on dialogue, humanitarian access, sovereignty, and rejection of military intervention aligns with its position. Côte d’Ivoire voted in favour of the actual February 2019 UNSC draft on Venezuela.
reasons.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic’s last-round position was support with no requested changes, and the balanced text aligns with its preference for humanitarian access, dialogue, democratic elections and respect for sovereignty. It therefore votes in favour and explains its support before the vote.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea's position is grounded in sovereignty and non-interference, and its red-line request on OP6 was rejected. It therefore maintains the abstention it signalled in the last negotiation round rather than supporting a US-led draft.
reasons.France: France supported the draft after its important OP4 change on elections without delay and full international observation was accepted. It aligns with France’s policy of backing humanitarian access and a peaceful democratic solution while opposing military intervention.
reasons.Germany: Germany supported the draft throughout negotiations and its position favours humanitarian access, human rights and a negotiated democratic solution while rejecting military intervention. It would therefore vote in favour and explain its vote before voting.
reasons.Indonesia: Indonesia historically abstained on the 28 February 2019 UNSC draft resolution on Venezuela, consistent with its emphasis on non-interference, sovereignty, and peaceful dialogue. Although its textual requests were accepted, overall concerns justified abstention rather than support.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait’s red-line request requiring the consent of the Maduro government for aid and observation was rejected, and Kuwait’s policy emphasizes sovereignty and non-interference. Its likely course is therefore to abstain and explain that decision.
reasons.Peru: Peru, as a Lima Group member, strongly opposed Maduro’s 2018 election and supported Guaidó, while prioritizing peaceful, sovereign and humanitarian-focused solutions. Its OP4 request was accepted, so Peru votes in favour.
reasons.Poland: Poland had already expressed support with changes, and its key request for new elections was accepted. A yes vote aligns with Poland’s pro-humanitarian, pro-democratic and EU/US-aligned position on Venezuela in February 2019.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia’s policy is to defend the Maduro government and the principle of non-interference, and it views the US-sponsored draft as an interventionist initiative. It would therefore vote against and exercise its veto.
reasons.South Africa: South Africa opposes the draft because its red-line demand on unilateral coercive measures and government consent was rejected, consistent with its sovereignty and non-interference policy. It would therefore vote against rather than abstain.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the compromise text, as its key requested changes were accepted, and it aligns with UK policy in favour of humanitarian access and a democratic, peaceful solution. Voting yes also reinforces Council support for legitimate elections while opposing external military intervention.
reasons.United States of America: The United States submitted this draft and strongly supports its objectives, including humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and a peaceful democratic path forward. Voting in favour is consistent with U.S. policy toward the Maduro regime and the Venezuelan crisis.

before.Belgium: Belgium votes in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because it responds to the urgent humanitarian needs of the Venezuelan people, calls for safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, and supports a peaceful, inclusive, Venezuelan-led political solution through free, fair, transparent and credible elections. The text also reaffirms Venezuela’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and rejects any threat or use of force. We urge all parties to protect civilians and to allow humanitarian assistance to reach those in need without politicization.
before.China: Mr. President, China has consistently maintained that the situation in Venezuela should be resolved through inclusive political dialogue by the Venezuelan people themselves, in full respect for Venezuela’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and the principle of non-interference in internal affairs. The draft before us remains unbalanced: it does not fully reflect the consent of and coordination with the Government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela on humanitarian assistance, it maintains externally prescribed electoral requirements, and it fails to address the harmful effects of unilateral sanctions. China therefore cannot support this draft and will vote against it. We call upon all parties to support peaceful dialogue, respect the legitimate authorities and institutions of Venezuela, and provide humanitarian assistance in accordance with humanitarian principles and with the consent of the receiving State.
before.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposal in operative paragraph 4. We support this resolution because it calls for an inclusive, Venezuelan-led and Venezuelan-owned dialogue without preconditions, with regional mediation where appropriate, and for free, fair and credible elections. It also demands safe and unimpeded humanitarian access while respecting Venezuela’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and the principle of non-interference, and it rejects any threat or use of force or external military intervention. Côte d’Ivoire will vote in favour.
before.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support its balanced emphasis on the urgent humanitarian needs of the Venezuelan people, safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, the cessation of violence, and a peaceful, inclusive, Venezuelan-led and Venezuelan-owned dialogue leading to free, fair, transparent and credible elections. We also welcome the text’s reaffirmation of sovereignty, territorial integrity and non-interference, and we urge all parties to pursue a peaceful solution in accordance with the Venezuelan Constitution and in full respect for the will of the Venezuelan people.
before.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea will abstain on this draft resolution. We remain deeply concerned by the humanitarian situation and the loss of life in Venezuela, and we call on all parties to renounce violence and allow neutral, unimpeded humanitarian assistance. However, my delegation has consistently upheld the principles of sovereignty, non-interference and the peaceful settlement of disputes. We regret that the draft does not fully reflect our red-line concerns, in particular the need to reject any external interference or attempt at regime change and to ensure that the crisis is resolved by Venezuelans themselves through inclusive dialogue, without external intervention. Humanitarian assistance must not be politicized or used as a pretext for interference. For these reasons, we abstain.
before.France: France votes in favour of this resolution. The humanitarian emergency in Venezuela requires safe, rapid and unimpeded access for aid, in accordance with humanitarian principles, and the crisis must be resolved through a peaceful, Venezuelan-owned political process leading to credible presidential elections without delay. We welcome that the text reaffirms Venezuela’s sovereignty and rejects any threat or use of force, and we call on all parties to cease violence and protect civilians.
before.Germany: Germany votes in favour of this resolution. The humanitarian emergency in Venezuela is deepening, and this Council must not remain silent while people lack food, medicine and basic services. We support immediate and unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians, and a peaceful, Venezuelan-led and Venezuelan-owned political solution leading to free, fair, transparent and credible elections. Germany stresses that this resolution rejects any threat or use of force and fully respects Venezuela's sovereignty, political independence and territorial integrity. We call on all Venezuelan actors to engage in good faith and to allow humanitarian assistance to reach those in need without political conditions.
before.Indonesia: Indonesia thanks the penholder for accepting some of our proposals, including the reference to non-interference and the voluntary nature of humanitarian assistance. Indonesia fully supports the humanitarian needs of the Venezuelan people and a peaceful, inclusive, Venezuelan-led dialogue. However, my delegation remains concerned that certain elements of the text could be perceived as going beyond the Council’s proper role and as external pressure on Venezuela’s internal affairs. For these reasons, Indonesia will abstain on this draft resolution. We urge all parties to refrain from violence, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and resolve the crisis through peaceful dialogue in full respect for Venezuela’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
before.Kuwait: Kuwait abstains. We strongly support humanitarian assistance and a peaceful, Venezuelan-owned solution to the crisis. However, the draft does not fully reflect the principles of sovereignty, non-interference and the consent of the host Government for humanitarian and electoral activities. We call on all parties to cease violence, protect civilians and allow safe humanitarian access in coordination with the United Nations and the Government of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, while pursuing an inclusive political dialogue without external interference.
before.Peru: Peru will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We welcome that the text reaffirms the sovereignty, political independence and territorial integrity of Venezuela and the principle of non-interference in internal affairs, while also rejecting any threat or use of force or external military intervention. Peru believes the Security Council must address the grave humanitarian situation and the need for a peaceful, Venezuelan-led, inclusive and credible solution, including free, fair, transparent and credible presidential elections without delay and the restoration of democratic institutional order, in accordance with the Venezuelan Constitution. We call on all parties to cease violence, protect civilians and allow safe, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access in accordance with humanitarian principles and without politicization.
before.Poland: Poland thanks the penholder for the revised draft and for accepting our request that the text clearly call for new free, fair, transparent and credible presidential elections. We remain deeply concerned by the humanitarian suffering, violence, and loss of life in Venezuela, including at the borders. We call on all parties to cease violence, protect civilians, and allow safe, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access in accordance with humanitarian principles. Poland also stresses that the crisis must be resolved peacefully, through an inclusive, Venezuelan-led dialogue without external interference and with full respect for Venezuela’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. The draft provides a balanced basis for the Council to support the Venezuelan people, and Poland will therefore vote in favour.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation cannot support this draft resolution and will vote against it. The text remains unbalanced and does not fully reflect the principle that the crisis in Venezuela must be settled by the Venezuelans themselves through inclusive national dialogue, without external interference or preconditions. We are particularly concerned that provisions on humanitarian assistance and elections could be used as a pretext for outside pressure and interference in Venezuela’s internal affairs. The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela has a sovereign right to determine its political, economic and social system and to manage its natural resources. We therefore oppose any attempt by the Security Council to impose external prescriptions, and we call for full respect for Venezuela’s sovereignty, political independence and territorial integrity.
before.South Africa: South Africa will vote against the draft resolution. While we remain deeply concerned by the humanitarian situation and by the violence in Venezuela, the text before us is unbalanced and does not address the serious impact of unilateral coercive measures, which exacerbate the suffering of the Venezuelan people. The draft also risks prescribing externally led political outcomes and does not adequately respect Venezuela’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and the principle of non-interference. South Africa supports a peaceful, inclusive and Venezuelan-led dialogue, with regional mediation where appropriate, and calls for humanitarian assistance to be delivered in accordance with humanitarian principles and without politicization or military pretext. The Security Council should act in a manner that helps create conditions for dialogue rather than deepen division.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. The humanitarian situation in Venezuela is grave, and this Council must speak clearly in support of unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians, full respect for human rights, and a peaceful, Venezuelan-owned political process leading to free and fair presidential elections. The text also reaffirms Venezuela’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and rejects the use of force. We urge all members to support it.
before.United States of America: The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. The Security Council cannot remain silent while the illegitimate Maduro regime blocks lifesaving humanitarian assistance and represses the Venezuelan people. We call on all parties to cease violence, allow safe and unimpeded humanitarian access, and move urgently toward free, fair, transparent and credible presidential elections that respect the will of the Venezuelan people. This Council must send a clear message that the Venezuelan people deserve democracy, dignity and humanitarian relief, and that further violence or external military intervention is unacceptable.

after.France: Mr President, France deeply regrets that this balanced draft resolution was not adopted. It responded to an urgent humanitarian emergency while reaffirming Venezuela’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and the principle of non-interference, and while rejecting any threat or use of force. The Council’s inability to act must not weaken our collective determination to help the Venezuelan people. France calls on all parties to cease violence, protect civilians, allow safe, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access without political conditions, and engage in a peaceful, inclusive, Venezuelan-led political process leading to free, fair, transparent and credible presidential elections without delay. France will continue to work with its partners to support a peaceful democratic solution to the crisis and will remain actively seized of the matter.
after.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation voted against this draft for the reasons we set out before the vote. Its rejection keeps the Security Council from being drawn into endorsing external prescriptions and attempts at unconstitutional regime change in Venezuela. The sponsors sought to use humanitarian concerns as a cover for political interference. Russia fully supports genuine humanitarian assistance in strict compliance with humanitarian principles, with respect for Venezuela’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and with the consent of its lawful authorities. The crisis in Venezuela must be resolved by Venezuelans themselves through inclusive national dialogue, without preconditions or outside interference. We call on all members to respect the UN Charter, refrain from threats and pressure, and support peaceful settlement efforts, including regional mediation mechanisms. We will continue to oppose any attempt to use this Council to interfere in the internal affairs of sovereign States.
after.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States is deeply disappointed that the Security Council has failed to adopt this balanced and urgent resolution. We thank the nine members who voted in favour. The two permanent members who cast vetoes today have chosen to shield an illegitimate regime and to deny the Venezuelan people the Council’s support for humanitarian access and a peaceful democratic path forward. Let us be clear: the Maduro regime is illegitimate, the 2018 election was neither free nor fair, and the democratic will of the Venezuelan people, expressed through the National Assembly and interim President Juan Guaidó, must be respected. The United States will not be deterred by this veto. We will continue to support the people of Venezuela, safe and unimpeded humanitarian assistance, the protection of civilians, and a peaceful return to democracy through free, fair, transparent and credible elections. The Council’s failure today does not weaken our resolve, and we will remain actively seized of this matter.
